rationale: Single replacement of the stem module boundary model.resnet.embedder (ResNetEmbeddings, group 3821cceac23fa97e5a55) per selection.json: an eager composite that micro-batches the frozen batch-32 request along the batch dimension. Baseline peak_allocated_bytes 280,169,472 B decomposes exactly as live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + out-of-place conv1 output 102,760,448 coexisting with the equally sized out-of-place batch_norm1 output + 8,622,944 workspace, all inside the stem; the parallel ReLU moment is the same 2x102,760,448 coexistence, so only attacking the conv->BN tier moves the peak. The replacement slices the contiguous [32,3,224,224] input into contiguous row chunks (no copies, no deduplication - all 32 rows execute), runs the unchanged sub-chain by calling the current parents through context.references (ResNetConvLayer 1dcfd07639d32233c49eafdf: conv2d->BatchNorm2d(eval)->ReLU; then MaxPool2d babacb997a72996bf303d028), assembles chunk results into one preallocated [32,64,56,56] tensor (25,690,112 B) and returns it to the untouched encoder stages - same shape, layout and values. No module.forward wrapper is installed by the candidate, no functional sites are declared, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies with no unrelated dispatch cost. Memory accounting at chunk 8: stem-internal peak = 46,758,048 + 19,267,584 + assembled output 25,690,112 + one chunk's conv_out + bn_out (2x25,690,112) = 143,095,968 B + workspaces, below the tier the unchanged stages set anyway. Honest expectation, correcting the selection's 143-152 MB estimate which omitted the second convolution's BatchNorm moment in stage 0: ResNetBasicLayer keeps residual (25,690,112) + layer[0] ReLU output (25,690,112) + layer[1] conv output (25,690,112) + layer[1] bn output (25,690,112) = 102,760,448 coexisting, so the post-optimization binding tier is 46,758,048 + 19,267,584 + 102,760,448 = 168,786,080 B (layer2.0 ties it: 25,690,112 + 6x12,845,056 = 102,760,448). Expected measured peak ~169-178 MB (tier + 3x3-conv workspaces), i.e. roughly -37% vs baseline; this is a hypothesis for the evaluator's clean samples, not a measured fact. Throughput: baseline median 7535.66 img/s (4.2465 ms), floor 7158.9 img/s (4.470 ms), headroom +224 us. Stem diagnostic CUDA time is 907.7/4156.2 us; its dominant kernels (bn_fw_inf 227.2 us, clamp/ReLU 217.8 us, max_pool 198.7 us) are bandwidth-bound with grids >=6272 blocks at batch 8 on the 128-SM 4090 and move identical total bytes, conv1's scudnn (262.5 us, grid 3136) may lose modest efficiency, plus ~15 extra launches, 4 assembly copies (25.7 MB total round-trip) and ~8 extra Python parent calls; even a 20% stem slowdown stays above 7158.9 img/s. Numerics: BatchNorm2d eval, ReLU and MaxPool2d are per-sample and value-exact under row chunking; conv2d is the identical aten op on contiguous slices with at most kernel-selection/reduction-order ulp effects far below the logits atol=rtol=1e-4, and a CPU replica of this exact composition is bit-identical to the parent stem. Coverage and contract: every inherited stem call still executes on each invocation (conv-layer and pooler subtrees 4x per invocation through context.references, their aten children and discovery record_function hooks firing per chunk); nothing is eliminated; no CUDA Graph capture or replay (replay would skip Python hooks and break runtime coverage per binding-contract); no state, caches or fixture-dependent outputs are retained - stateless eval-mode inference recomputes from the live input every call, with the framework's synchronize boundaries and the whole project measured unchanged. Guards: the chunked path applies only to the observed compatible signature (4-D cuda float32 contiguous 3-channel non-requires-grad input, batch > chunk, eval mode); anything else, kwarg-only calls, and any runtime exception inside the chunked path fall back to the parent reference with distinct record_route labels (stem_microbatch_rowsN / stem_single_chunk / stem_parent_signature_fallback / stem_parent_runtime_fallback:<ExcType>); missing build-time references return an empty mapping, a concise setup-failure category that leaves the parent installed. No inputs/previous-feedback.txt and no inputs/previous-candidate/ exist, so this is the first attempt with nothing to reconcile. Optional tunable stem_chunk_rows (default 8) lets the TaskSearch/TPE loop trade launch overhead for stem transient without touching frozen semantics; chunk 4 keeps the ~168.8 MB stage tier with 8 chunks, chunk 16 halves launches at ~194.5 MB stem-limited peak (46,758,048 + 19,267,584 + 25,690,112 + 2x51,380,224) - both still far below baseline.

setup_work.build_time_gpu_work: none: build(context) only resolves context.references/context.modules, reads stem_chunk_rows from context['parameters'] and returns one closure; no tensors are allocated, no parameters are transformed, no model state changes, no fixture-dependent precomputation
setup_work.first_invocation_behavior: the chunked path allocates its tensors through the normal CUDA caching allocator during the framework's 2 warmup invocations, so the recurring chunk-sized blocks (three 25,690,112 B transients per chunk at batch 8, 25,690,112 B assembled output, 6,422,528 B pooled chunks) are already cached when the 5 timed repeats run; reset_peak_memory_stats() sees allocator reuse, not cudaMalloc storms
setup_work.memory_scope: no CUDA Graph capture and no allocation migration: every stem allocation stays inside the measured peak_allocated_bytes counter, and no retained graph pools are created; expected per-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes ~169-178 MB vs baseline 280,169,472 with framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes improving accordingly since no invocation exceeds the run peak; setup adds nothing, and reserved-pool behavior is outside the objective and not claimed as a saving

quality_risks: Numerics: cudnn may select a different conv1 kernel at batch 8, reordering the 147-term accumulation and producing ulp-level logits differences; quality requires full 1000-class logits within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 - expected to hold comfortably (BatchNorm(eval)/ReLU/MaxPool are value-exact under row chunking and a CPU replica of the composition is bit-identical), but only the evaluator's reference comparison against offline-reference semantics decides

Throughput: if batch-8 scudnn efficiency loss plus the 4x launch and assembly-copy overhead exceeds the +224 us headroom over the 4.2465 ms baseline, images_per_second could fall below the 7158.9 floor; the declared stem_chunk_rows=16 parameter is the fallback (2 chunks, fewer launches, ~194.5 MB peak) and is itself a large memory improvement over baseline

Fallback semantics: any exception inside the chunked path re-executes the whole stem through the parent reference (idempotent under eval/inference_mode, no state mutated) and self-reports stem_parent_runtime_fallback:<type>; guards route unexpected signatures, kwargs, non-contiguous/odd-dtype/CPU/requires-grad inputs and training mode to the parent with stem_parent_signature_fallback, so adversarial or unseen calls preserve exact parent behavior

Coverage: the only replaced boundary is the stem module; all 17 selection-listed stem-subtree call IDs keep executing (subtree invocation count 1->4 per invocation at chunk 8), so quality coverage and runtime traces still observe the inherited conv/bn/relu/maxpool work; no calls are eliminated and no counter is filled with unused work

params.name: stem_chunk_rows
params.description: Contiguous rows per stem micro-batch within the frozen batch-32 request (remainder chunks handled generically; batch, workload and semantics unchanged). 8 (default) and 4 both keep the stem below the unchanged stage tiers (~168.8 MB binding floor); 16 halves launch overhead at a ~194.5 MB stem-limited peak.
